method: delta audit on top of the v0.9.5 audit: every v0.9.5 source citation (path, line, symbol) remapped through the v0.9.5..v0.9.7 diff and its line text re-checked; every outcome whose cited function, reject builder or helper changed re-read in both trees; new/removed status, body, header, gRPC-status, close-code and rejection-phase literals diffed per file; manual source audit + grep, not a completeness proof (docs/audit/gateway-0.9.7-delta.md)

headers.name: X-Gateway-Error
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:40281 (H1/H2 backend-response builder); src/proxy/mod.rs:48115 (build_response_with_gateway_error: overload/config_stale); src/proxy/mod.rs:280-302 (circuit-breaker/overload/config-stale reject maps, lowercase x-gateway-error); src/proxy/mod.rs:25354 restore_authoritative_gateway_error_header; src/proxy/mod.rs:25386 insert_x_gateway_error_for_backend_failure (H3: src/http3/server.rs:10598,16423; src/http3/cross_protocol.rs:10100); src/plugins/adaptive_concurrency.rs:26
headers.semantics: Closed 7-token vocabulary (src/retry.rs:212-238, byte-identical to v0.9.5): connection_failure, backend_timeout, backend_error, circuit_breaker_open, overload, config_stale, concurrency_limit. On backend-dispatch responses derived only from (connection_error, final status): connection_error -> connection_failure; status 504 -> backend_timeout; status >=500 -> backend_error; else absent (src/retry.rs:281). overload is also forced on the response-transformer output-ceiling 502 (src/proxy/mod.rs:25340). Never on 2xx/3xx/4xx from the gateway core; never on native-gRPC trailers-only siblings of the overload/config_stale fences. v0.9.6+ (released v0.9.7): the route-deadline 504 {"error":"Request timeout"} (src/proxy/mod.rs:49270 route_request_timeout_response, connection_error=false) carries backend_timeout even when the deadline expired before any backend got the request (error_class dispatch_policy_rejected); the native HTTP/3 route-timeout refusal 503 carries none.
headers.spoofing_notes: Partially protected. Backend copies are stripped and replaced on the plain HTTP-family backend-response builders (H1/H2 src/proxy/mod.rs:40270; H3 via src/proxy/mod.rs:25377 apply_authoritative_backend_gateway_error_header). No strip was found on the native gRPC response builders (buffered src/proxy/mod.rs:37411-37451 passes backend headers through sanitize_client_response_headers_for_wire, which only removes hop-by-hop/framing fields), so a gRPC backend can inject X-Gateway-Error. NOT stripped from plugin reject header maps (only the adaptive_concurrency and CB/transformer paths restore it authoritatively), so an operator/custom plugin or reject-path header decorator can emit any value on a gateway rejection. Any non-Ferrum endpoint can send it.

headers.name: X-Gateway-Upstream-Status
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:40285 (builder .header append when upstream_is_fallback); src/http3/server.rs:10418-10419 (H3: retain+insert only when is_fallback)
headers.semantics: Only value 'degraded': load balancer used the all-unhealthy (or unhealthy-subset -> parent) fallback. May accompany any status including 2xx.
headers.spoofing_notes: H1/H2 builder path does not strip a backend-supplied X-Gateway-Upstream-Status when the gateway did not use fallback, and appends a second line when it did (no retain before .header()). H3 only strips it when is_fallback.

headers.name: gateway-error-reason
headers.semantics: Undocumented gateway-authored reason on some DispatchPolicyRejected 502s. Values seen: 'backend_tls_sni_requires_direct_h2', 'backend-egress-policy-denied' (H3 bridge only), mesh reasons such as 'mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target', 'Unix socket retry dispatch is unavailable', 'HBONE transport or gateway identity is unavailable for retry target'.
headers.spoofing_notes: Not in any strip list (src/proxy/headers.rs:745 is_backend_response_strip_header).

headers.name: Via
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:40338 (backend-response builder); values built at src/proxy/mod.rs:9784-9792 from FERRUM_ADD_VIA_HEADER (default true, src/config/env_config.rs:4970) and FERRUM_VIA_PSEUDONYM (default 'ferrum-edge', :4971); H3 src/http3/server.rs:10411
headers.semantics: '1.1 ferrum-edge' / '2.0 ferrum-edge' / '3.0 ferrum-edge' (protocol of the upstream response). Written on responses that pass through the backend-response builder, including gateway-synthesized 502/504 backend failures (buffered => '1.1 <pseudonym>'); NOT written on pre-dispatch gateway rejections built by build_response / build_response_from_normalized_reject (404, 401, 405, 431, 503 overload/config_stale, CB 503). Backend Via hops are retained and the gateway hop appended.
headers.spoofing_notes: A backend can send 'Via: 1.1 ferrum-edge' itself; operators can rename or disable it.

headers.name: Alt-Svc
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:40291 via ProxyState::alt_svc_for_frontend_port (src/proxy/mod.rs:10647; value built at :9777 'h3=":<FERRUM_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT>"; ma=86400' when HTTP/3 enabled); v0.9.6+ withholding: RouteTimeoutAltSvc (src/proxy/mod.rs:6647), route_timeout_withholds_alt_svc (:10670)
headers.semantics: Advertises HTTP/3 on backend-path responses when enable_http3. v0.9.6+ (released v0.9.7): withheld on every frontend port that serves a mesh_route_dispatch rule with request_timeout_ms or attempt_timeout_ms (Gateway API HTTPRoute timeouts.request / timeouts.backendRequest), re-derived per configuration generation; withheld on ALL ports when such a rule is Global-scoped or attached to a proxy without listen_port. Its absence therefore does not mean HTTP/3 is disabled.
headers.spoofing_notes: Backend alt-svc is not stripped; gateway value is appended.

headers.name: Allow
headers.semantics: Route 405: route allowed_methods uppercased, ', '-joined, config order. Protocol 405: 'GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS'.
headers.spoofing_notes: Only on gateway-built 405s; policy cannot alter it. A backend's own 405 Allow passes through untouched.

headers.name: Connection: close
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:40331 (drain / keepalive pressure / RED shedding on any response); src/proxy/mod.rs:30417 (framing observer 400); src/proxy/h1_framing_guard.rs:82-84 (parse envelopes)
headers.semantics: HTTP/1.1 only. On ordinary responses indicates gateway drain or overload pressure (probabilistic under RED), not an error.
headers.spoofing_notes: Hop-by-hop; backend Connection header is stripped (src/proxy/headers.rs:745) so a close seen by the client comes from the gateway or an intermediary.

headers.name: x-adaptive-concurrency-limit / x-adaptive-concurrency-inflight
headers.semantics: Only when the adaptive_concurrency plugin has expose_headers enabled and a TargetLimit rejection occurs.
headers.spoofing_notes: Plain names, not stripped from backend responses.

headers.name: WWW-Authenticate
headers.writer: src/plugins/utils/auth_flow.rs:731 reject() (401 + mechanism challenge); src/proxy/mod.rs:29539 missing_authentication_reject (fallback value); src/plugins/basic_auth.rs:226; src/plugins/ldap_auth.rs:91; src/plugins/oauth2_introspection.rs:1429
headers.semantics: On 401 only. Values seen: 'Basic realm="ferrum-edge", charset="UTF-8"' (basic_auth, ldap_auth), 'Bearer' (oauth2_introspection), and the literal fallback 'ferrum-edge' when no credential was presented and no applicable mechanism advertises a challenge (body {"error":"Authentication required"}). DPoP/jwks challenges: see plugin outcomes.
headers.spoofing_notes: Backend WWW-Authenticate passes through on proxied 401s; realm ferrum-edge / bare 'ferrum-edge' is a strong but forgeable Ferrum-like marker.

headers.name: x-request-id (request id)
headers.semantics: No request-id header is emitted by the gateway core. Only when the correlation_id plugin is enabled on the route: header x-request-id by default (configurable header_name), echoed on responses including plugin rejections by default. Accepts an incoming value from the client if present (not audited in detail).
headers.spoofing_notes: Only a correlation aid; not a provenance or authorization token.

headers.name: Content-Type: application/json
headers.semantics: All gateway JSON errors use {"error":"..."} bodies (some add "limit" or "message"). Not a Ferrum identifier by itself. Exception: the backend-failure bodies built by the backend-dispatch builders (502 Backend unavailable / Backend DNS resolution failed / Backend response body read failed / Backend response body exceeds maximum size, 503 Response buffering capacity exceeded / Backend connection limit exceeded, 504 Backend timeout, and the route-deadline 504 Request timeout) carry no Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 path (empty header map; lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7). Plugin rejects and admission fences do carry application/json.

headers.name: grpc-status / grpc-message (gateway-generated)
headers.semantics: Trailers-Only HTTP 200, content-type application/grpc, empty body. HTTP reject status mapped by src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307.
headers.spoofing_notes: Backends legitimately send grpc-status; no provenance marker distinguishes gateway-authored gRPC errors.

headers.name: Server
headers.semantics: Ferrum sets no Server header (no writer found in src/proxy or src/http3); a Server header seen by the client is the backend's or an intermediary's.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-*
headers.semantics: X-Ferrum-* names in the source are admin-API (e.g. X-Ferrum-Namespace-Unserved, src/admin/mod.rs:2411), internal plugin handoff markers stripped before the wire (x-ferrum-original-content-encoding, grpc-web bridge markers), or mesh request markers. None is a client-facing proxy response header at v0.9.7, except the mesh-only x-ferrum-mesh-tunnel-reuse: fenced on an HBONE CONNECT 200 (v0.9.6+, src/proxy/hbone_proxy.rs:1411, name at src/modes/mesh/hbone.rs:47), which only a peer mesh proxy sees; it advertises a capability and is not a diagnostic marker.

headers.name: Content-Security-Policy
headers.semantics: v0.9.6+ (released v0.9.7): "default-src 'none'; sandbox" on spec documents served by spec_expose (also on HEAD); not on its fetch-error responses. Not a diagnostic marker.
headers.spoofing_notes: Any backend can send a Content-Security-Policy on its own responses; only its presence on a spec_expose document is gateway-authored.

error_class_semantics.typical_http: 502 Backend DNS resolution failed (reqwest) or Backend unavailable (pools)
408 body read timeout / 499 internal / auth-expiry 401 placeholder
502 Backend response body exceeds maximum size
502 Backend unavailable (H3 pre-header) / WS normal close
502 Backend unavailable (pools); reqwest lane uses 503 + dispatch_policy_rejected instead

grpc_reject_status_mapping.note: Gateway-generated native-gRPC rejects are HTTP 200 Trailers-Only (content-type application/grpc, grpc-status, grpc-message); grpc-message comes from the reject header, else the JSON body's grpc_message/message/error/details field (mod.rs:25491).

rejection_phases_operator_only.note: rejection_phase is transaction-log metadata only (never a response header). Values found in log_*rejected_request call sites of src/proxy/mod.rs and src/http3/*.rs; token_for_rejection_phase (src/retry.rs:318) maps circuit_breaker_open|circuit_breaker|adaptive_concurrency|overload|config_stale to metric tokens.

drift.client_visible_effect: None: src/retry.rs, src/proxy/headers.rs, src/proxy/stream_error.rs, src/proxy/response_buffer_budget.rs, src/proxy/auth_lifetime.rs and src/plugins/utils/openai_error.rs are byte-identical. ErrorClass::ALL (19), the 7 X-Gateway-Error tokens, their derivation (http_observability_error_class), request_reached_wire, should_retry and the response-header strip list are unchanged. http_reject_status_to_grpc_status is byte-identical (moved src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2225 -> :2307). Wire libraries: rustls 0.23.40 -> 0.23.45; hyper 1.9.0, h2 0.4.19, h3 0.0.8, quinn 0.11.9, reqwest 0.13.3, tungstenite 0.28/0.29 unchanged; hyper-util 0.1.20 is now vendored with a Ferrum patch.
drift.evidence: cmp of the named files between the tags; Cargo.lock of both tags
drift.anvil_impact: Token vocabulary, token scope/owner rules and the 5xx-only marker rule apply to both releases unchanged.

drift.client_visible_effect: None. Every source citation of the 0.9.5 catalog was remapped through the diff's line map (1212 of 1216 onto unchanged lines, text-identical); the 4 citations that landed in changed hunks (WAF finish_timeout, parse_redis_failure_policy) were re-cited by hand. Embedded path:line references in prose were remapped the same way; bare line numbers were mapped by hand.
drift.evidence: diff line map of each cited file; text equality of the cited line in both trees
drift.anvil_impact: sha 8fed134 on every citation.

drift.client_visible_effect: Gateway API HTTPRoute rule timeouts (projected onto mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms / attempt_timeout_ms; no such rule exists at v0.9.5, default none). HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2: the total deadline ends the request with a new 504 {"error":"Request timeout"} + X-Gateway-Error: backend_timeout, whether the backend held the attempt (error_class read_write_timeout) or not (dispatch_policy_rejected: still uploading, hooks, DNS, admission, retry backoff); the per-attempt budget ends with the existing 504 {"error":"Backend timeout"}; a body still streaming at either deadline is cut (HTTP/2 reset, HTTP/1.1 close) keeping Content-Length. gRPC folds both into the RPC deadline: 'Deadline exceeded at gateway' (grpc-status 4) or, for a post-send attempt expiry on H1/H2, 'Backend deadline exceeded'. Native HTTP/3 refuses plain requests on such rules with 503 {"error":"Route request timeout is not supported over HTTP/3"} (no gRPC variant is reachable), and Alt-Svc is withheld on ports serving such rules.
drift.evidence: src/proxy/mod.rs:48962 ROUTE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_BODY, :49270 route_request_timeout_response, :49291 route_deadline_expiry_response; src/proxy/body.rs:1047 with_route_request_deadline; src/plugins/mod.rs:4379 arm_route_request_deadline; src/http3/server.rs:4708, :18296; src/proxy/mod.rs:6647, :10647
drift.anvil_impact: A 504 backend_timeout may never have reached a backend (the token finding says so for this release). 'Deadline exceeded at gateway' no longer proves the caller's own grpc-timeout fired. Only for Gateway API / mesh_route_dispatch rules with timeouts.

drift.client_visible_effect: Gateway API HTTPRoute rule retry: listed statuses retried for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/DELETE, pre-wire failures retried for every method, fixed backoff (default 100 ms). No new status, body or header: the client sees only the final attempt.
drift.anvil_impact: More hidden retries behind a single response on Gateway-API-configured routes; Anvil's dispatch findings already never claim a single upstream attempt.

drift.client_visible_effect: v0.9.5: a pooled HTTP/1 backend connection that closes at enqueue time strands the request until backend_read_timeout_ms, then 504 {"error":"Backend timeout"} + backend_timeout although nothing reached the backend. v0.9.7: replayed transparently on a new connection when the stranded one was reused (any method, nothing was sent), otherwise an immediate 502 {"error":"Backend unavailable"} + connection_failure (connection_pool_error). Same for HBONE inner HTTP/1 and Unix-socket HTTP/1 backends.
drift.anvil_impact: The 0.9.5-only token note ('a pooled HTTP/1.1 connection closing at the wrong moment can hold a request until the read timeout') is not shown for 0.9.7 profiles.

drift.client_visible_effect: scan_budget_ms never skips a body or WebSocket-message scan any more and hits always decide first, so an enforcing hit over budget still rejects (v0.9.5 could forward an unscanned body under scheduler load with the default log_and_allow). on_scan_timeout gains fail_closed (403 on a clean over-budget body scan only where an enforcing body policy applies; WebSocket: close 1008 'message could not be inspected'). Status/body/close codes unchanged.
drift.evidence: src/plugins/waf/mod.rs:633 run_body_scan_with_budget, :686 finish_scan, :1056 finish_timeout, :2096 parse_timeout_action; src/plugins/waf/websocket.rs:436
drift.anvil_impact: Same public signals; the WAF 403 stays ambiguous with bot_detection.

drift.client_visible_effect: rate_limiting redis_failure_policy default flips fail_closed -> local_fallback: a Redis outage no longer yields the 503 {"error":"Rate limit enforcement is temporarily unavailable"} by default but per-process quotas (ordinary 429s, or the local-capacity 429). graphql and grpc_method_router keep fail_closed. Request-quota Redis clients (rate_limiting, graphql, grpc_method_router) now require the TIME command (+time ACL); without it the endpoint is unavailable and redis_failure_policy decides. Redis counting is a 16-sub-bucket trailing window with refund-on-refusal (different 429 boundary timing and x-ratelimit-remaining values; same 429 bytes, still no Retry-After). graphql / grpc_method_router consumer keys are tagged consumer:/ip:.
drift.evidence: src/plugins/utils/rate_limit.rs:95-104 parse_redis_failure_policy, :2447 check_http_windows_redis; src/plugins/utils/redis_rate_limiter.rs:4415 probe_server_time; src/plugins/graphql.rs:500; src/plugins/grpc_method_router.rs:467
drift.anvil_impact: Absence of the 503 during a Redis outage is the 0.9.7 default; 429 timing expectations must be release-scoped.

drift.client_visible_effect: jwt_auth, jwks_auth and the OIDC callback reject a token whose iss is not a single JSON string (array, null, number, object), with the existing bodies: 401 {"error":"Invalid JWT token"}, 401 {"error":"Invalid or unrecognized JWT"}, 400 {"error":"Invalid ID token"}. v0.9.5 accepted an array iss containing the configured issuer.
drift.anvil_impact: Same bodies, wider condition; lab scenario AUTH-009.iss-array checks the release-dependent verdict.

drift.client_visible_effect: oauth2_introspection honours a future integer nbf from the provider: new 401 {"error":"Token is not yet valid"} + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token" (gRPC 16); a non-integer nbf is 503 {"error":"Token introspection unavailable"}; null is absent. v0.9.5 ignored nbf.
drift.anvil_impact: New distinct 401 body only in the 0.9.7 catalog.

drift.client_visible_effect: An ID token (or JWT) with a fractional exp is now read as a NumericDate: OIDC sessions from such tokens expire at that exp (401 challenge / browser redirect earlier than before), and jwt/jwks credentials get a lifetime deadline (long-lived WebSocket/streaming/gRPC sessions cut at exp). Signals unchanged.
drift.anvil_impact: None on signal matching; timing only.

drift.client_visible_effect: mcp_gateway reserves its scope case-insensitively and for '%'-suffixed tails: /MCP, /Mcp/x, /mcp%2e now get 404 'Unknown MCP endpoint' (JSON-RPC -32600) instead of passing through to the backend. Correction to the v0.9.5 catalog's drift note: /mcp/ with endpoint.path /mcp was already this 404 at v0.9.5 (matches_endpoint exact, src/plugins/mcp_gateway.rs:1213 @20e7603); the #5536 trailing-slash alias existed only between the tags.
drift.anvil_impact: A case-variant MCP path is a gateway 404 on 0.9.7 and a backend response on 0.9.5.

drift.client_visible_effect: spec_expose responses gain Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox (also on HEAD; not on fetch errors).
drift.anvil_impact: Header presence differs by release.

drift.client_visible_effect: bot_detection allow_list entries that start or end with punctuation now match (word-boundary anchors only at word-character edges), so some User-Agents 403'd by v0.9.5 pass. The 403 body is unchanged.
drift.anvil_impact: Fewer 403s for such allow lists; signal unchanged.

drift.client_visible_effect: response_caching, request_deduplication and ai_semantic_cache keys bind the matched route's response-header transforms and route-override backend TLS/DNS policy: entries no longer replay across such rules, and every key misses once after the upgrade. HIT/MISS header values unchanged.
drift.anvil_impact: A MISS after an upgrade or rule change is expected on 0.9.7.

drift.client_visible_effect: ai_stream_router (Anthropic provider) validates reasoning_effort: unsupported values get 400 'Invalid request for Anthropic translation: unsupported reasoning_effort' (param reasoning_effort, code invalid_reasoning_effort) where v0.9.5 silently dropped the field; adaptive thinking.display summarized|omitted is now accepted (v0.9.5: 400 invalid_thinking). Not in the CHANGELOG.
drift.anvil_impact: Same body family (openai_error), new detail/code.

drift.client_visible_effect: Two ai_federation invalid_request messages quote the tool name with double quotes instead of single quotes; status, type and code unchanged.
drift.anvil_impact: Message text only.

drift.client_visible_effect: TCP/TLS relays, WebSocket tunnel mode and HBONE byte tunnels flush a buffering (TLS) writer before parking; TCP/TLS relays keep backend_write_timeout_ms armed across the flush and the half-close, so a TLS backend that stops draining ends with 'backend write inactivity timeout' where v0.9.5 could hang. The client still sees a reasonless close. WebSocket tunnel mode arms no backend write timeout, so it gains the flush but no new close.
drift.anvil_impact: L4/WS stall fixtures may close on 0.9.7 where 0.9.5 hung; public signal unchanged.

drift.client_visible_effect: Mesh only. The HBONE 403 bodies {"error":"HBONE tunnel requires an authenticated mesh peer"} / {"error":"HBONE UDP tunnel requires an authenticated mesh peer"} already existed at v0.9.5 for unauthenticated peers (correction to the v0.9.5 drift note); v0.9.7 also returns them when an authenticated peer's chain no longer verifies against the trust in force or is revoked. Live tunnels are revoked (reasonless end) when a later policy/trust publication would refuse them. mesh_outbound_registry (REGISTRY_ONLY) never enforces on Inbound listeners (its 502 rejects existed at v0.9.5 but were uncatalogued).
drift.anvil_impact: Mesh peers only; not relevant to ordinary API clients.

drift.client_visible_effect: Uncatalogued at v0.9.5: an enabled response_transformer drops the backend trailer section on trailer-forwarding paths. v0.9.7 narrows it for rules-free route-override consumers to requests whose matched rule published a response-header override.
drift.anvil_impact: Missing trailers remain unattributable from the client.

drift.client_visible_effect: Not a gateway change: corrections to data carried over from the v0.9.5 audit, applied to both catalogs. (1) 15 native-gRPC records had grpc_status 13 while their audited grpc-status was 3, 4, 7, 8 or 14 (or variable); grpc_status now equals the audited value, or null when it varies. (2) Gateway backend-failure bodies (502 Backend unavailable / Backend DNS resolution failed / body read failed / body too large, 503 Response buffering capacity exceeded / Backend connection limit exceeded, 504 Backend timeout) carry no Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 path: the builders use an empty header map, observed live over HTTP/1.1 on both releases (UP-001, UP-002, UP-009, UP-010, UP-013, UP-014, UP-015, UP-018, UP-020, GW-019-ERROR); the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json.
drift.evidence: src/proxy/mod.rs:43695 http_backend_dispatch_error_response (headers: HashMap::new()), :43947 backend_dns_resolution_failed_response; lab records results/lab/<stamp>-{core,admission,policy,tls}/<ID>.record.json on v0.9.5 and v0.9.7
drift.anvil_impact: None on matching: other_headers is never matched, and the corrected gRPC records carry no body pattern, so they could not match a response before or after the fix; documentation accuracy only.

matrix_seed_reconciliation.source: docs/handoff/FERRUM_ANVIL_FAILURE_MATRIX.json source_class_seed_coverage / public_header_seed_coverage vs v0.9.5 code, re-checked against v0.9.7

notes.dns_lookup_error/UP-001: public body is path-dependent: reqwest preflight 'Backend DNS resolution failed' vs pools 'Backend unavailable'
notes.tls_error/UP-004,UP-006: backend mTLS on the reqwest HTTP/1 pool surfaces as connection_pool_error (connection_failure) or connection_reset (backend_error), not tls_error
notes.read_write_timeout/UP-009..011: identical public 504 pair; streamed UP-011 is a truncated body, not a 504
notes.connection_pool_error/UP-016: v0.9.7: the stranded pooled HTTP/1 request race of v0.9.5 is fixed; a fresh connection fails at once as 502 connection_failure (connection_pool_error, upstream.pool.dispatch_canceled) and a reused one is replayed transparently, so UP-016 never yields the delayed 504 on this release
notes.backend_connection_limit/UP-018: reqwest lane yields 503 'Backend connection limit exceeded' + backend_error with class dispatch_policy_rejected; the class only exists on direct-H2/H3/gRPC/HBONE pools
notes.graceful_remote_close/PROTO-009: for WebSocket this is a log class only; the client sees the relayed peer Close
notes.config_stale/GW-005: requires DP mode, lost CP, age > FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS (3600) and FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=fail_closed; readiness_only produces no client signal
notes.overload/GW-002,GW-003,GW-009: overload and drain are byte-identical; GW-009 is 502 with {error,limit} body

marker_semantics.note: Release-specific sentences Anvil adds to its marker findings (ferrum.token.<token>, ferrum.marker.absent) when a trusted profile declares this compatibility id. The wording in catalog/diagnostics/findings.en.json stays release-neutral, so a profile whose compatibility id has no catalog gets only the meaning every audited release shares.

backend_timeout.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.7 any 504, including a backend's own, carries this value, and a route's total request timeout (Gateway API HTTPRoute timeouts.request) can end a request with a 504 before any backend received it.

backend_error.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.7 it is attached to 5xx responses the backend returned itself, to failures the gateway observed talking to the backend, and to some gateway-only refusals (response-buffer capacity, HTTP/1.1 in-flight limits, egress-policy denials, response-phase policy rejections).
backend_error.source: src/retry.rs:281-287 (unchanged); outcomes gateway.capacity.response_buffer, upstream.h1_pending_limit.reqwest, upstream.egress_denied_literal_ip, generic.response_phase_5xx.x_gateway_error (unchanged at v0.9.7)

absent.explanation: On Ferrum Edge 0.9.7 plugin rejections carry no X-Gateway-Error value.
absent.source: headers[X-Gateway-Error].semantics; plugin reject path src/proxy/mod.rs:25802 normalize_reject_response_with_provenance adds none (unchanged)

removed_outcomes.reason: The v0.9.5-only stranded pooled HTTP/1 request race (504 backend_timeout after backend_read_timeout_ms although nothing reached the backend) no longer exists: v0.9.7 vendors hyper-util 0.1.20 with patch hyper-util-001 (vendor/hyper-util-0.1.20-ferrum-patched) and adds src/proxy/h1_send_release.rs for HBONE inner and Unix-socket HTTP/1, so the request is replayed on a new connection when the stranded one was reused, or fails at once as upstream.pool.dispatch_canceled (502 {"error":"Backend unavailable"} + connection_failure, error_class connection_pool_error) on a fresh one (#5714, #5719, #5720).

outcomes.condition: reqwest-dispatched request (HTTP/1.1 backend, H2-via-reqwest, H3->reqwest bridge) whose preflight DnsCache resolution of the backend host fails (not an egress-policy denial).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports it could not resolve the configured backend host name from the gateway; the request was not sent to any backend.

outcomes.condition: Backend Content-Length exceeds the effective max response body size (FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES default 10485760, or route response_size_limiting), or a buffered body grows past it.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response replacing backend status

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the upstream response because it exceeds the gateway's configured response size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend crashed or returned 502.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: page or reduce the response; gateway operator: review the response size limit for this route.
outcomes.notes: gRPC buffered path maps ResponseTooLarge through the gRPC trailers-only mapping (see protocol outcomes). Streaming without Content-Length is enforced mid-stream instead (streaming.response_size_exceeded_mid_stream). No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-014; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked.

outcomes.condition: Process-wide retained-response budget (FERRUM_RESPONSE_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, default 256 MiB) cannot admit a buffered response that is within every per-response ceiling.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response replacing backend status; gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 8 grpc-message 'Response buffering capacity exceeded'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked gateway memory budget to buffer this response; the backend answered but its response was not delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is unhealthy or returned 503 (despite X-Gateway-Error: backend_error), or that retrying elsewhere helps immediately.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review FERRUM_RESPONSE_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES and why responses are buffered.
outcomes.notes: Doc says 'Do not reuse backend_error for a response that never reached a backend' but this gateway-local refusal carries backend_error (status 503>=500, connection_error=false). Body is the only public discriminator. Not retried by the gateway. No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-015; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked.

outcomes.condition: Aggregate buffered-request budget (FERRUM_REQUEST_BUFFER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, default 256 MiB) cannot admit another buffered upload.

public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response; gRPC trailers-only grpc-status 8 'Request buffering capacity exceeded'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked gateway memory budget to buffer this request body; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request body is too large or that the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review request buffering budget and plugins that force buffering (WAF, validators, retries).
outcomes.notes: X-Gateway-Error is path-dependent: absent when built by build_request_buffer_capacity_response (pre-dispatch builder), but 'backend_error' when the same refusal returns through the backend-dispatch seam (request_buffer_capacity_backend_response).

outcomes.condition: Aggregate request-decode (decompression inspection) budget cannot admit the working set for a governed request.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked capacity to inspect (decode) this request body; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request is malformed or the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review request decode budget.
outcomes.notes: Emitted as a plugin-style reject; X-Gateway-Error presence not confirmed per path.

outcomes.condition: reqwest (HTTP/1.1) lane: DestinationRule connectionPool.tcp.maxConnections reached for the destination; no socket opened.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to open another connection to this upstream because a gateway-configured connection ceiling is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is down or returned 503 (despite backend_error).
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review maxConnections for this destination.
outcomes.notes: Same condition on direct-H2/H3/gRPC pools surfaces as 502 'Backend unavailable' + connection_failure (upstream.connection_limit.pooled). WebSocket upgrade path uses the same 503 body (mod.rs:15245). No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 backend-response path: the gateway builds this body with an empty header map (lab-observed over HTTP/1.1 on 0.9.5 and 0.9.7: UP-018; the v0.9.5 audit had recorded application/json). The HTTP/3 writer was not lab-checked.

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule connectionPool.http.http1MaxPendingRequests reached for the backend (upstream overflow) on the reqwest lane.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge shed this request because a gateway-configured in-flight request limit for the upstream is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned 503 or is unhealthy.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff; gateway operator: review http1MaxPendingRequests.
outcomes.notes: Carries backend_error although no backend was contacted.

outcomes.condition: Literal-IP backend (or dns_override) blocked by the backend egress policy; no dial.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to contact the configured backend address because gateway egress policy blocks it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned an error or is down.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: fix the backend address or egress allow/deny policy.
outcomes.notes: H3 cross-protocol bridge additionally sets gateway-error-reason: backend-egress-policy-denied (src/http3/cross_protocol.rs:1618).

outcomes.condition: reqwest dispatch where proxy dns_override conflicts with a literal-IP backend URL host.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"backend DNS override cannot be applied to literal target"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the route's DNS override cannot be applied to the configured literal backend address (gateway configuration issue).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: correct the route's dns_override/backend host.

outcomes.condition: Backend TLS SNI override that neither the direct-H2 pool nor the reqwest dial can honor.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the route's backend TLS server-name override cannot be honored on this path (gateway configuration issue).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend certificate is wrong or the backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: review the BackendTLSPolicy/SNI override and backend protocol.
outcomes.notes: gateway-error-reason is an undocumented gateway-authored response header; it is NOT stripped from backend responses, so it is spoofable.

outcomes.condition: Mesh-only: target requires HBONE / sidecar mTLS / Unix-socket transport that is unavailable for this attempt.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Bad Gateway","message":"Mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target"} | {"error":"Bad Gateway","message":"Unix socket retry dispatch unavailable"}
public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response; gRPC trailers-only UNAVAILABLE

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the secured mesh transport required for this backend was unavailable.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend application failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway/mesh operator: check gateway mesh identity and transport availability.
outcomes.notes: Mesh deployments only; included for completeness. Reason strings include 'mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target', 'Unix socket retry dispatch is unavailable', 'HBONE transport or gateway identity is unavailable for retry target'.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned a complete 5xx response other than 504 (connection_error=false).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The response was relayed by Ferrum Edge with a 5xx status that, per the gateway's coarse marker, came from or after the upstream exchange; the marker alone does not prove the backend application authored it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway failed, or (without body/provenance evidence) that the application itself produced it: several gateway-local refusals also carry backend_error.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: inspect backend logs for this request; compare body with known gateway bodies.
outcomes.notes: Backend-supplied X-Gateway-Error values are stripped and replaced on this path (mod.rs:40270).

outcomes.condition: Backend itself returned a complete 504 response (e.g. an upstream load balancer timeout).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A 504 was relayed through Ferrum Edge and marked backend_timeout; the marker is also applied when the backend itself answered 504, so only the body distinguishes it from the gateway's own timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway timed out (unless the body is exactly {"error":"Backend timeout"} or, on v0.9.6+, {"error":"Request timeout"} from a trusted Ferrum destination).
outcomes.remediation: API owner/infra behind the gateway: check the backend's own upstream timeouts.
outcomes.notes: http_observability_error_class keys backend_timeout on status 504 alone, not on ErrorClass. v0.9.6+: the gateway-authored route-deadline 504 carries {"error":"Request timeout"} (upstream.route_request_timeout.*); a backend can send either literal body.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned 1xx-4xx (including its own 401/403/404/429).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The upstream application's response was relayed; no gateway failure marker is present.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That a 401/403/404/429 came from the gateway (gateway plugin rejections use the same statuses).
outcomes.remediation: Treat as application result unless other provenance says otherwise.
outcomes.notes: Any X-Gateway-Error the backend sets is stripped on H1/H2/H3 backend-response paths.

outcomes.condition: All targets in the upstream (or selected subset) were unhealthy; the load balancer used the all-unhealthy / parent-upstream fallback. Any final status.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports it routed this request in degraded mode because no upstream target was considered healthy; the request itself may still have succeeded.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request failed, or which target was used.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator/API owner: investigate health-check failures for the upstream.
outcomes.notes: Spoofing: on the H1/H2 builder path a backend-supplied X-Gateway-Upstream-Status is NOT stripped when the gateway did not use fallback, and when it did, the builder appends a second field line. H3 replaces it only when is_fallback. Treat as spoofable.

outcomes.condition: Data-plane mode: last applied CP snapshot older than FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS (default 3600) with CP authority lost and FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=fail_closed (default).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 grpc-message 'Gateway configuration stale' WITHOUT X-Gateway-Error. TCP/UDP listeners: accepted socket dropped / datagram session refused (no payload).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused new work because its data plane has not received a fresh configuration from its control plane within the allowed window; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the client payload, credentials, or the backend are at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: restore control-plane connectivity / config sync; client can retry later (not dispatched).
outcomes.notes: Runs before routing, plugins and overload admission. Already-accepted connections drain. Readiness also degrades (/health ready:false). On the HTTP/3 frontend the native-gRPC variant DOES carry x-gateway-error: config_stale (protocol.grpc.config_stale_h3), and the H3 overload fence runs before this one. WebSocket upgrades get the HTTP 503. FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=readiness_only produces no client signal.

outcomes.condition: Overload manager critical request pressure (FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS with FERRUM_OVERLOAD_REQ_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD default 0.95) OR shutdown drain started (SIGTERM).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 'Service overloaded' without X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to admit this request because the gateway process is shedding load or is draining for shutdown; no upstream was contacted for this request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is unhealthy, that it is CPU overload specifically, or which of overload vs shutdown drain applied.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff (safe: request was not dispatched); gateway operator should check overload manager pressure and deployment/shutdown activity.
outcomes.notes: Drain and overload produce byte-identical responses; drain/pressure additionally add 'connection: close' to other responses (mod.rs:40311-40331). FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS defaults to 0 (request-based shedding off). HTTP/3 native-gRPC variant carries x-gateway-error: overload (protocol.grpc.overload_h3). On HTTP/2 a drain also sends GOAWAY(NO_ERROR) via hyper graceful_shutdown.

outcomes.condition: Critical connection pressure (reject_new_connections) or the listener connection semaphore (FERRUM_MAX_CONNECTIONS, default 100000) exhausted; for TCP listeners also the stale-config fence.

public_signal.transport: accepted TCP socket dropped immediately before TLS/HTTP (code comment says 'TCP RST'; kernel may emit FIN or RST)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The connection to the gateway endpoint was closed before any TLS or HTTP response; this is consistent with gateway connection admission (overload, connection limit, stale config for L4) but also with any network middlebox or a non-listening service.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That Ferrum refused it (no Ferrum marker is possible here), or any HTTP status.
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff; compare with a direct health check; gateway operator can check reject/connection-limit counters.
outcomes.notes: No HTTP response possible. H3 equivalent: QUIC Incoming.refuse() (src/http3/server.rs:1146).

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker for the proxy/target is open (or half-open probe slot taken).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: normalized to trailers-only grpc-status 14 (503->UNAVAILABLE) with grpc-message 'Service temporarily unavailable (circuit breaker open)'; x-gateway-error header is restored into the reject header map so it is expected on gRPC too (not lab-verified).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected this attempt at its circuit breaker because recent failures to this upstream exceeded the configured threshold; this attempt was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That no earlier retry attempt in the same request reached a backend, or that the backend is still failing now.
outcomes.remediation: Wait for the breaker cooldown and retry; API owner/gateway operator: investigate the upstream's recent failures.
outcomes.notes: Runs through after_proxy reject hooks (headers may be decorated) then the token is restored authoritatively. rejection_phase=circuit_breaker_open in logs.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_IP (default 0 = off) exceeded for the resolved client IP.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Too many concurrent requests from this IP"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge limited this request because too many requests from the same client IP were in flight at once.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That an API rate-limit quota (rate_limiting plugin) was exhausted.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce concurrency from this IP; no Retry-After is provided.
outcomes.notes: Pre-routing; no plugins run; no Retry-After / rate-limit headers; gRPC not specially mapped here (plain JSON).

outcomes.condition: Connection authenticated with a client certificate whose trust decision was withdrawn by an accepted client-CA/CRL reload (issue #3857).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 16 'Client certificate trust withdrawn'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge no longer trusts the client certificate this connection was established with; new requests on it are refused.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API credential/token is wrong.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reconnect with a currently trusted client certificate; operator: check client CA/CRL changes.

outcomes.condition: HTTPS (H1/H2): the request carries Early-Data: 1 (added by a trusted CDN per RFC 8470) and its method is not in the configured early-data method list. HTTP/3: the request stream was accepted while the QUIC handshake was still in progress (0.5-RTT window, listener with FERRUM_TLS_EARLY_DATA_METHODS and no frontend mTLS) and its method is not in that list; checked before routing, so no proxy_id is logged.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 14

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to process this request as TLS 0-RTT early data; resend it after the handshake completes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the method is unsupported by the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller/CDN: retry without early data.
outcomes.notes: Anvil lab `early` (EARLY-002, EARLY-006) observes both paths with the same public signal. The HTTP/3 listener classifies any request stream accepted before its handshake-completion signal as early data (accept polling is biased ahead of that signal), so a 1-RTT request racing the handshake can also draw this answer.

outcomes.condition: No proxy route matched the request host/path.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12 grpc-message 'Not Found'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The endpoint answered 404 with Ferrum's route-miss body shape; if the destination is a trusted Ferrum gateway this means no gateway route matched this host/path.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That every 404 is a gateway route miss (backends can return the same bytes), or that the resource does not exist in the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check host, path prefix and scheme against the published API; gateway operator: check route configuration.
outcomes.notes: Pre-plugin: no auth/CORS plugins run, so a browser CORS failure may mask it. No Via header on this gateway-built response.

outcomes.condition: Route matched but the method is not in the route's allowed_methods.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The route exists but does not accept this HTTP method; the Allow header lists the accepted methods.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That authentication failed or the resource is missing.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: use one of the methods in Allow.
outcomes.notes: rejection_phase=allowed_methods (logs only). Allow is gateway-authoritative (policy cannot alter it).

outcomes.condition: TRACE request, or CONNECT that is not a WebSocket extended CONNECT (and not HBONE).

other_headers.Allow: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"TRACE method is not allowed"} | {"error":"CONNECT method is not allowed"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge blocks this HTTP method at the protocol level for all routes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the route does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: do not use TRACE/CONNECT through the gateway.

outcomes.condition: Request with application/grpc content-type using a method other than POST.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only gRPC response (400 mapped to INVALID_ARGUMENT)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the gRPC call because gRPC requires POST.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the service/method does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send gRPC calls with POST.
outcomes.notes: Logged/metric status is 400.

outcomes.condition: One request header (name+value bytes) exceeds FERRUM_MAX_SINGLE_HEADER_SIZE_BYTES (default 16384).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request header '<name>' exceeds maximum size of <limit> bytes"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because one header is larger than the gateway allows; the body names the header.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: shrink the named header (often cookies or tokens).
outcomes.notes: Header name echoed (JSON-escaped). H1 parser buffer floor is 8 KiB above which hyper itself may reject first (see frontend_parse.hyper_default_rejects).

outcomes.condition: Sum of request header bytes exceeds FERRUM_MAX_HEADER_SIZE_BYTES (default 32768).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its headers are larger in total than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce header size.
outcomes.notes: On HTTP/1 a head larger than the hyper parser buffer (max(limit, 8 KiB)) is rejected by hyper before this check with hyper's own response.

outcomes.condition: Number of header fields exceeds FERRUM_MAX_HEADER_COUNT (default 100).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because it has more header fields than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer headers.

outcomes.condition: path+query length exceeds FERRUM_MAX_URL_LENGTH_BYTES (default 8192).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request URL length (<n> bytes) exceeds maximum of <limit> bytes"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its URL is longer than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the resource is missing.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: shorten the URL / move data into the body.

outcomes.condition: Query parameter count exceeds FERRUM_MAX_QUERY_PARAMS (default 100).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because it has more query parameters than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected a parameter value.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer query parameters.

outcomes.condition: Request body exceeds the effective limit (FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES default 10485760, FERRUM_MAX_GRPC_RECV_SIZE_BYTES default 4194304 for gRPC, or a lower route/request_size_limiting limit) while buffering or by Content-Length.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 8 'Request body exceeds maximum size of <limit> bytes'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its body exceeds the gateway's size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend received the full body (for streamed uploads the backend may have received a truncated prefix).
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce the payload or use a chunked/multipart upload API; operator may review the limit.
outcomes.notes: The request_size_limiting plugin uses a different body shape ({"error":...,"limit":N}); see plugin outcomes. For streamed uploads exceeding the limit mid-stream the backend receives a truncated upload; client-visible shape depends on path (not fully audited).

outcomes.condition: Client upload stalled beyond the request body read timeout while the gateway was buffering it.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 4 'Request body read timed out'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge stopped waiting for the rest of the request body from the client; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend timed out.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check local upload throughput / proxy; operator: review request body timeout.

outcomes.condition: Client disconnected/aborted while the gateway was buffering its request body.

public_signal.transport: normally never observed by the client (it already disconnected)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The client side ended the upload before the gateway received the full request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway or backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check local cancellation/network.
outcomes.notes: 499 is a gateway-internal status recorded in logs/metrics.

outcomes.condition: Request smuggling / desync checks on headers: HTTP/1.0 with Transfer-Encoding, both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, invalid/non-numeric/overflowing/conflicting Content-Length, H2/H3 with Transfer-Encoding, invalid TE, missing/duplicate/invalid Host on HTTP/1.1.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request contains both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers"} | {"error":"HTTP/1.0 does not support Transfer-Encoding"} | {"error":"Content-Length header contains invalid empty value"} | {"error":"Content-Length header contains invalid non-numeric value"} | {"error":"Content-Length header exceeds supported integer range"} | {"error":"Multiple Content-Length headers with conflicting values"} | {"error":"Request contains multiple Host headers"} | {"error":"HTTP/1.1 request is missing a Host header"} | {"error":"Host header contains invalid empty value"} | {"error":"Host header contains invalid characters"} | {"error":"HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 do not support Transfer-Encoding"} | {"error":"TE header contains invalid empty value"} | {"error":"TE header must be 'trailers' or absent"} | {"error":"TE header contains invalid characters"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed or ambiguous at the HTTP protocol layer before routing; the body names the rule.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected the payload or that authentication failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request framing/Host/path encoding shown in the body (often a client or intermediate proxy bug).
outcomes.notes: No X-Gateway-Error on protocol 400s (issue #4543).

outcomes.condition: Host header and :authority disagree, are invalid, missing, or malformed.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Host header contains invalid authority"} | {"error":"Request authority contains invalid authority"} | {"error":"Host header and request authority disagree"} | {"error":"Request contains multiple Host headers"} | {"error":"Request is missing both :authority and Host"} | {"error":"Host header contains invalid characters"} | {"error":"Request contains malformed Host or authority"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed or ambiguous at the HTTP protocol layer before routing; the body names the rule.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected the payload or that authentication failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request framing/Host/path encoding shown in the body (often a client or intermediate proxy bug).
outcomes.notes: No X-Gateway-Error on protocol 400s (issue #4543).

outcomes.condition: Request path contains an ambiguous percent-encoding the canonical policy path refuses (GHSA-69xf-42xm-4w4f): incomplete/double-encoded escapes, encoded '/' or '\\', literal backslash, encoded control chars, (encoded) dot segments.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request path contains an incomplete percent-escape"} | {"error":"Request path contains a double-encoded percent-escape"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded path separator"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded backslash"} | {"error":"Request path contains a backslash"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded control character"} | {"error":"Request path contains an unrepresentable percent-escape"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded dot segment"} | {"error":"Request path contains a dot segment"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed or ambiguous at the HTTP protocol layer before routing; the body names the rule.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected the payload or that authentication failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request framing/Host/path encoding shown in the body (often a client or intermediate proxy bug).
outcomes.notes: No X-Gateway-Error on protocol 400s (issue #4543). gRPC / gRPC-Web get grpc-status 3 with messages like 'Encoded path separator in request path' (src/policy_path.rs:228).

outcomes.condition: First HTTP/1 head on a connection has conflicting Content-Length values, HTTP/1.0+Transfer-Encoding, or an invalid UTF-8 request-target; written directly to the socket before hyper sees the request.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Multiple Content-Length headers with conflicting values"} | {"error":"HTTP/1.0 does not support Transfer-Encoding"} | {"error":"Malformed HTTP request"}
public_signal.transport: raw 'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request' envelope then connection close

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed HTTP/1 framing before any routing and closed the connection.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend saw the request.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the client's HTTP/1 framing.
outcomes.notes: Only for the connection's first head before any response byte; later malformed heads get hyper's empty-bodied 400 (docs/error_classification.md:224-272). Before any RequestContext: no plugins/logs rows, no X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: The inbound HTTP/1 framing observer could not verify framing (state unknown/overflowed).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"HTTP/1 request framing could not be verified; connection will be closed"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge could not verify this HTTP/1 connection's request framing and closed it defensively.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request content was invalid.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: retry on a fresh connection; report if persistent.

outcomes.condition: Other malformed HTTP/1 heads hyper rejects at parse time (truncated head, non-numeric Content-Length hyper refuses, oversized head beyond the parser buffer, later heads on a pipelined connection).

public_signal.body_shape: empty body (hyper automatic response; 431 possible for an oversized head — hyper behaviour, not Ferrum code)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server rejected the request as unparseable HTTP before any application handling.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That Ferrum specifically generated it (no Ferrum body/header marker is present) or any gateway policy decision.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request format.
outcomes.notes: Exact hyper status/body per failure kind is library behaviour and must be lab-verified; not Ferrum-authored.

outcomes.condition: Established TCP relay ends: backend reset/close, idle timeout (tcp_idle_timeout_seconds), backend write timeout, authorization lifetime expiry, drain. v0.9.7 (#5588/#5676): each relay direction flushes a buffering writer (e.g. a TLS leg) before parking on its reader, and backend_write_timeout_ms stays armed while accepted bytes are still held by the writer and across the half-close until poll_shutdown resolves.

public_signal.transport: client sees FIN (half-close preserved for graceful backend FIN) or connection close/reset; no reason is transmitted

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway stream connection closed without delivering application data or a reason; L4 proxies cannot report the cause in-band.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause (backend down, policy reject, breaker, timeout) or that the backend received data.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: check the stream transaction log (error_class, disconnect_cause, disconnect_direction) for this connection.
outcomes.notes: Timing change vs v0.9.5: a TCP+TLS relay whose TLS writer accepted bytes without sending them could stall indefinitely (both sides waiting) in v0.9.5; v0.9.7 flushes, so such exchanges now proceed, and a writer that still cannot drain now trips backend_write_timeout_ms ('backend write inactivity timeout') instead of hanging until the idle timeout (or forever with tcp_idle_timeout_seconds=0). A failed half-close with bytes still owed is now logged as a write-side failure rather than a clean completion. Wire signal (FIN/close/reset, no reason) unchanged. Same pump serves WebSocket tunnel mode and HBONE byte tunnels.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A gateway-side plugin (possibly a custom one) returned this response; without the plugin's own documentation its meaning cannot be derived from the source audit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Any specific built-in cause, or that the backend produced it, or that an X-Gateway-Error value on this response is gateway-core authored.
outcomes.remediation: Ask the gateway operator for the custom plugin's contract; add a signed/schema-validated local rule extension if needed.
outcomes.notes: PluginFailurePolicy (FailClosed / KeepLastKnownGood / OptionalFailOpen, src/plugins/mod.rs:1302-1310) governs only construction/reload failures, not runtime rejects; there is no runtime 'plugin error' status. Hooks return PluginResult, not Result, so there is no request-time plugin-error channel and no per-hook HTTP timeout (gRPC calls end at the client deadline with grpc-status 4 'Deadline exceeded at gateway'). Release builds use panic = "abort" (Cargo.toml:461), so a panic in any plugin kills the whole gateway process and resets every in-flight connection; there is no generic 500. A custom plugin that produces response bodies without declaring response_body_production surfaces as 503 {"error":"Response buffering capacity exceeded"}. See also plugin.custom.* records.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge shed this request at its adaptive concurrency limit for the upstream; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API applied a rate limit, or that the backend crashed (the limit adapts to observed backend latency/errors, so the backend may be slow).
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff (no Retry-After is sent); gateway operator/API owner: check upstream latency and adaptive_concurrency settings.

outcomes.notes: Initial-response header policy plugins may add headers. Pre-routing errors use build_grpc_error_response (no policy). Clients must read the END_STREAM HEADERS as terminal even if a NO_ERROR reset follows.
