outcomes.condition: The gateway's RPC deadline expires before a stream was acquired, during buffered upload, or while a buffered response/rejection is still uncommitted (replaces it). The deadline is the client grpc-timeout (as capped/defaulted by a grpc_deadline policy) and, since v0.9.6 (released v0.9.7), a matched Gateway API HTTPRoute rule timeouts.request / mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms folded in (earlier wins); a rule's timeouts.backendRequest / attempt_timeout_ms also ends here when it expires before the request was sent to the backend, and on native HTTP/3 at any point.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200; any buffered backend response is discarded [grpc-message: Deadline exceeded at gateway]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gRPC deadline in force at the gateway (the caller's grpc-timeout, possibly capped by gateway policy, or a route-configured request/attempt timeout) expired before a response was delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend slowness as proven cause, or that the caller's own grpc-timeout was the deadline that fired (a route rule timeout produces the identical signal).
outcomes.remediation: Caller: raise grpc-timeout if one was sent or reduce work; operator/API owner: check route rule timeouts (HTTPRoute timeouts.request/backendRequest, mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms/attempt_timeout_ms).
outcomes.notes: Overrides an already-selected plugin/backend error. v0.9.7: route rule timeouts fold into the RPC deadline for gRPC and gRPC-Web on H1/H2/H3 (plugins/mod.rs:4379); the remaining budget is sent upstream as grpc-timeout, so a deadline-aware backend may instead return its own DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (protocol.grpc.backend_status_passthrough). No Ferrum marker distinguishes a route timeout from a client grpc-timeout on the wire.

outcomes.condition: The gateway's RPC deadline (client grpc-timeout / grpc_deadline policy, or since v0.9.6 a folded route timeouts.request or the committed attempt's timeouts.backendRequest budget) fires after response HEADERS were sent but before any response DATA.

public_signal.transport: backend HEADERS then synthesized TRAILERS frame with END_STREAM (percent-encoded message) [grpc-message: Deadline%20exceeded%20at%20gateway]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gRPC deadline in force at the gateway expired after the backend answered with headers but before any message was delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend error, or that the caller's own grpc-timeout (rather than a route-configured timeout) was the deadline that fired.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: review deadline; operator: review route rule timeouts.
outcomes.notes: Backend body dropped. gRPC-Web gets an encoded trailer DATA frame. H3 relay: trailers if 0 DATA offered else RESET_STREAM(H3_INTERNAL_ERROR) (src/http3/server.rs:14247). v0.9.7: a route rule timeout folded into the RPC deadline produces the same terminal.

outcomes.condition: The gateway's RPC deadline (client grpc-timeout / grpc_deadline policy, or since v0.9.6 a folded route timeouts.request or the committed attempt's timeouts.backendRequest budget) fires after response DATA was already sent.

public_signal.transport: stream reset, no trailers (H2 RST_STREAM code chosen by hyper, INTERNAL_ERROR inferred; H3 H3_INTERNAL_ERROR)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The RPC stream was reset after messages were delivered; no terminal gRPC status was received.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, a specific grpc-status, or which party caused the reset.
outcomes.remediation: Treat the RPC as incomplete.
outcomes.notes: No terminal status is fabricated once DATA was sent. v0.9.7: route rule timeouts folded into the RPC deadline end the stream the same way.

outcomes.condition: Buffered backend gRPC response exceeds the max response body size.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused a buffered gRPC response larger than its response size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend crash.
outcomes.remediation: Reduce response size or raise the limit.
outcomes.notes: H3 frontend message: 'Response payload exceeded limit' (cross_protocol.rs:7859).

outcomes.condition: Client gRPC request body exceeds FERRUM_MAX_GRPC_RECV_SIZE_BYTES (default 4194304) or route limit, detected before response headers.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: gRPC request payload size exceeds maximum of {N} bytes]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the gRPC request because its payload exceeds the gateway's gRPC receive limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend rejection.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send smaller messages.
outcomes.notes: Streaming overflow path forwards 'gRPC request payload size exceeds maximum' (mod.rs:34627). Overflow after response headers not traced.

outcomes.condition: Non-size error while collecting a buffered gRPC request body.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: Failed to read gRPC request body: {GrpcProxyError Debug}]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway failed while reading the client's gRPC request body.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check client stream; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Embeds a Rust Debug rendering; match on the prefix only.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: credential expiry or authenticated-stream max lifetime reached before the response head is committed.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: credential expired | authenticated stream lifetime reached]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway ended the gRPC call because the caller's credential (or maximum authenticated lifetime) expired while the call was in progress.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the credential was invalid at submission.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: refresh credentials.
outcomes.notes: Non-gRPC gets 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"} (auth.authorization_lifetime_expired_before_commit).

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: credential/lifetime expiry after HEADERS but before DATA.

public_signal.transport: synthesized TRAILERS grpc-status 16 [grpc-message: credential expired | authenticated stream lifetime reached]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway ended the gRPC stream with UNAUTHENTICATED because the caller's credential or maximum authenticated lifetime expired.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend authorization failure.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: refresh credentials and reconnect.
outcomes.notes: Plain HTTP/SSE never gets trailers (see streaming.authorization_lifetime_expired_after_commit).

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: backend stream error/reset or per-frame idle read timeout after response HEADERS were forwarded.

public_signal.transport: frontend RST_STREAM (hyper chooses the reason: inner h2 Reason if present, else INTERNAL_ERROR); no grpc-status trailers synthesized

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The RPC stream was reset after response headers; no terminal gRPC status was received, so the outcome is unknown.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, a specific grpc-status, or that the gateway authored the failure.
outcomes.remediation: Treat as incomplete; retry only idempotent RPCs.
outcomes.notes: A gRPC client typically reports INTERNAL or CANCELLED from its own library mapping; the missing trailer is the evidence.

outcomes.condition: Backend returns its own gRPC outcome (any grpc-status).

public_signal.transport: backend HTTP status, grpc-status, grpc-message, grpc-status-details-bin forwarded; only hop-by-hop trailer names stripped

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A grpc-status other than those synthesized by the gateway, delivered with backend headers, is the backend's RPC outcome relayed unchanged.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway authored it.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: inspect service logs.
outcomes.notes: If the backend omits grpc-status, UNKNOWN(2) is recorded in log metadata only; nothing is synthesized. Native gRPC response path adds neither X-Gateway-Error nor alt-svc.

outcomes.condition: Gateway failed to build the gRPC client response.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway failed internally while building the gRPC response.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Reject-builder fallback at mod.rs:26224 uses 13 with the same message.

outcomes.condition: Mesh only: target needs a mesh transport or Unix socket the direct gRPC pool cannot dial.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: fixed mesh refusal messages (e.g. 'gRPC to a unix-socket backend cannot be dialed directly', 'HBONE dispatch required for this backend target: {reason}')]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused to dispatch this gRPC call because the required mesh transport is unavailable.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: transport/identity.
outcomes.notes: Mesh deployments only.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC backend literal IP denied by the backend egress policy.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: backend address blocked by egress policy]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused to contact the configured gRPC backend address because gateway egress policy blocks it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: egress policy.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: a protected response representation could not be inspected.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: response representation could not be inspected]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway withheld the gRPC response because a gateway response policy could not inspect it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend returned INTERNAL.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: response policy / encoding.

outcomes.condition: Pre-routing header-size (431), per-IP concurrency (429) and protocol-header (400) rejections on a gRPC request.

public_signal.body_shape: same JSON bodies as the HTTP outcomes
public_signal.transport: plain HTTP response even for gRPC clients (not trailers-only)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway rejected the gRPC call at the HTTP layer before gRPC handling (header limits, per-IP concurrency, or protocol header rules), so the gRPC client saw a non-gRPC HTTP error.
outcomes.must_not_claim: The grpc-status the client library synthesized from the HTTP status.
outcomes.remediation: Inspect the HTTP status/body; fix headers or concurrency.
outcomes.notes: gRPC clients will apply their own HTTP-to-status mapping (typically UNAVAILABLE/INTERNAL/UNKNOWN), which hides the real cause.

outcomes.condition: gRPC over the HTTP/3 frontend: backend dispatch fails before response headers.

public_signal.transport: H3 trailers-only HEADERS(200)+FIN [grpc-message: BackendUnavailable=>14 'Service unavailable'; BackendTimeout=>4 'Backend deadline exceeded'; ClientDeadlineExceeded=>4 'Deadline exceeded at gateway'; ResourceExhausted=>8 'Request payload exceeded backend limit'; ResponseTooLarge=>8 'Response payload exceeded limit'; ResponseBufferCapacity=>8 'Response buffering capacity exceeded'; Internal=>13 'Internal gateway error'; malformed client trailers=>3 'Malformed request trailers']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Over HTTP/3 the gateway reports a gRPC upstream failure before response headers with the listed status/message; the backend may or may not have received the call.
outcomes.must_not_claim: The exact failed step beyond the message.
outcomes.remediation: Retry only idempotent RPCs.
outcomes.notes: Messages differ from H1/H2 ('Backend unavailable', 'Resource exhausted', Internal=>14).

outcomes.condition: Any gateway gRPC error for a gRPC-Web request; also backend responses lacking grpc-status on translated gRPC-Web.

public_signal.body_shape: gRPC-Web trailer frame (0x80 flag) carrying grpc-status/grpc-message; base64 for grpc-web-text
public_signal.transport: HTTP 200 with body-framed trailers [grpc-message: same mapping and messages as native gRPC]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: gRPC-Web errors arrive as HTTP 200 with a body-framed trailer carrying grpc-status.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success from HTTP 200.
outcomes.remediation: Decode the trailer frame.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_CONNECTIONS (default 20000) or per-IP WebSocket limit reached.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade because its WebSocket connection limit (global or per client IP) is reached.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; operator: WebSocket limits.
outcomes.notes: Global and per-IP limits send identical bytes; no X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Origin header not in the route's allowed_ws_origins.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade because the Origin is not allowed for this route.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Authentication failure.
outcomes.remediation: Use an allowed Origin or ask the operator.

outcomes.condition: Credential expiry elapsed before the WebSocket upgrade completed.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The caller's credential expired before the WebSocket upgrade completed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Invalid credential at submission.
outcomes.remediation: Refresh credentials.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS (default 3600) elapsed before upgrade completed.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway's maximum WebSocket lifetime elapsed before the upgrade completed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry; operator: lifetime settings.

outcomes.condition: Backend WebSocket dial fails (DNS, TCP, TLS, connect timeout) OR the backend answered the upgrade with a non-101/200 status.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway could not establish the upstream WebSocket (connect/DNS/TLS failure or the backend refused the upgrade); the backend's own response is not shown.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which of these happened, or that the backend is down (it may have answered the upgrade with an error).
outcomes.remediation: Operator: gateway logs; API owner: backend upgrade handling.
outcomes.notes: Backend's own rejection status/body is NOT relayed; no 504 variant; no X-Gateway-Error. H3 sends {"error":"DNS resolution for backend failed"} for DNS failures.

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule maxConnections reached for the WebSocket backend.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the upgrade because a gateway-configured backend connection ceiling is reached.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; operator: maxConnections.
outcomes.notes: Same body as the reqwest HTTP lane but without X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Gateway-internal WebSocket upgrade failure.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Internal server error during WebSocket upgrade"} | {"error":"Invalid backend path coordinates"} | {"error":"WebSocket request buffering invariant violated"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway failed internally during the WebSocket upgrade.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: logs.

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker open or adaptive_concurrency shed on a WebSocket upgrade (overload/config_stale pre-routing fences also apply).

public_signal.body_shape: the same JSON bodies as the HTTP admission outcomes

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade at an admission fence named by X-Gateway-Error; the upgrade was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later.
outcomes.notes: Only these four pre-upgrade WebSocket rejects carry X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Gateway policy close mid-session: credential expired, maximum lifetime, client trust withdrawn, fragmented-message limit (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_INCOMPLETE_MESSAGE_FRAMES 1024 / _SECONDS 60), ws_rate_limiting, WAF message block.

public_signal.transport: Close frame sent to both peers (bounded 100 ms write), then teardown [ws close reason: "credential expired | maximum lifetime reached | client trust withdrawn | fragmented message limit | <ws_rate_limiting close_reason, default 'Frame rate exceeded'> | message rejected by security policy | message exceeds inspectable size | message could not be inspected"]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket for a policy reason given in the close reason (credential/lifetime/trust, fragment limit, rate limit, or WAF).
outcomes.must_not_claim: An application-level error, or a policy other than the stated reason.
outcomes.remediation: Act on the close reason: refresh credentials, slow down, or change message content.
outcomes.notes: The reason string distinguishes the policy. Tunnel mode (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_TUNNEL_MODE) sends no Close frame.

outcomes.condition: Gateway drain/shutdown or idle timeout (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 300).

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers [ws close reason: 'gateway draining | idle timeout']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket because it is draining or the session was idle.
outcomes.must_not_claim: An application error.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; send keepalives if idle.
outcomes.notes: A relay failure racing the drain also becomes 1001 'gateway draining'.

outcomes.condition: Frame > FERRUM_MAX_WEBSOCKET_FRAME_SIZE_BYTES (default 16 MiB) or message > 4x that; or ws_message_size_limiting ceiling.

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers (either direction) [ws close reason: "'' (global limit) | <plugin close_reason, default 'Message too large'>"]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A WebSocket frame or message exceeded a gateway size limit and the session was closed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Protocol corruption, or which direction violated it without logs.
outcomes.remediation: Send smaller messages/frames.
outcomes.notes: Direction-dependent class: request_body_too_large (client->backend) or response_body_too_large (backend->client).

outcomes.condition: Transport failure on either relay half (e.g. backend TCP reset / I/O error).

public_signal.transport: Close frame written to the surviving peer [ws close reason: 'relay error']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket because relaying to the other side failed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which side failed or why.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Does not say which side failed.

outcomes.condition: RFC 6455 protocol violation by either peer.

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers [ws close reason: 'protocol error']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket with a protocol error; a peer violated RFC 6455 (or, unverified, the backend dropped TCP without a Close handshake).
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which peer misbehaved.
outcomes.remediation: Check client and backend WebSocket framing.
outcomes.notes: Inferred, unverified: a backend TCP FIN without a Close handshake may surface in tungstenite as Protocol(ResetWithoutClosingHandshake) and therefore 1002 rather than 1011.

outcomes.condition: A peer (normally the backend) sends a Close frame.

public_signal.transport: peer Close code and reason forwarded verbatim

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A Close code not in the gateway's set (1001/1002/1008/1009/1011 with the gateway's reasons) was relayed from the backend unchanged.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway authored it.
outcomes.remediation: Interpret per the application's close codes.
outcomes.notes: If a gateway policy Close was already published, the policy Close wins.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_TUNNEL_MODE=true (H1/H2, no frame plugins): lifetime, drain or trust stop.

public_signal.transport: raw transport dropped without a Close frame (client libraries typically report 1006)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The WebSocket transport ended without a Close frame.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause, or that 1006 was transmitted by a peer.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: No size/fragment/WAF/rate closes in tunnel mode. v0.9.7 (#5588): server-first / reply bytes that a WSS (tokio-rustls) client leg accepted but could not yet encrypt under backpressure are flushed instead of held until the next write or the idle-timeout drop; tunnel mode arms no backend write timeout, so no new close path was added.

outcomes.condition: RFC 9220 WebSocket over HTTP/3 when FERRUM_HTTP3_WEBSOCKET_ENABLED is false.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"WebSocket over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: WebSocket over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 WebSocket.

outcomes.condition: Gateway shutdown (HTTP/2 connections).

public_signal.transport: GOAWAY; in-flight streams continue; new streams on the connection meanwhile get the overload 503 [h2: NO_ERROR (GOAWAY, hyper)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server announced graceful connection shutdown (GOAWAY NO_ERROR); streams above last-stream-id were not processed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: TLS failure or that in-flight streams failed.
outcomes.remediation: Open a new connection.
outcomes.notes: Library behaviour; FERRUM_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS (default 30) bounds the process drain.

outcomes.condition: Authenticated stream expired and the client did not drain the terminal, or client-cert trust withdrawn for the TLS connection.

public_signal.transport: GOAWAY then TCP hard close after 2 s (AUTHORIZATION_TRANSPORT_CLOSE_SETTLE, mod.rs:14681); sibling streams can die [h2: NO_ERROR (GOAWAY, hyper)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server sent GOAWAY and closed the connection.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; if repeated with long streams, check credential expiry.

outcomes.condition: Client opens more concurrent streams than advertised SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The stream was refused because the client exceeded the server's advertised concurrent stream limit; the request was not processed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Respect SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
outcomes.notes: Ferrum only configures the limit.

outcomes.condition: Client triggers too many pending-accept or local-error resets (rapid reset).

public_signal.transport: GOAWAY + connection close [h2: ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM (GOAWAY; h2 library behaviour)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server closed the connection for excessive stream resets.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Fix client stream reset behaviour.
outcomes.notes: Unverified library code.

outcomes.condition: reject_new_connections overload flag or listener draining (QUIC).

public_signal.transport: QUIC handshake refused [h3: QUIC transport CONNECTION_REFUSED (quinn Incoming::refuse)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The QUIC handshake was refused by the server, consistent with gateway overload or drain.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Network blocking with certainty.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later or fall back to TCP.
outcomes.notes: Library code.

outcomes.condition: Gateway shutdown, or overload keepalive-pressure tier rising (one-shot GOAWAY per connection).

public_signal.transport: H3 GOAWAY then connection close after drain [h3: GOAWAY; later streams H3_REQUEST_REJECTED (vendored h3); on shutdown CONNECTION_CLOSE app code 0x0100 H3_NO_ERROR reason 'shutdown']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server announced graceful HTTP/3 shutdown or connection shedding; later streams were rejected unprocessed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Failure of in-flight streams.
outcomes.remediation: Open a new connection.
outcomes.notes: H1/H2 instead get 'connection: close' on responses.

outcomes.condition: Client-cert trust withdrawn for the QUIC connection.

public_signal.transport: QUIC application CONNECTION_CLOSE; all streams fail [h3: H3_REQUEST_REJECTED (0x010B) CONNECTION_CLOSE, reason 'client certificate trust withdrawn']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the QUIC connection because the client certificate is no longer trusted.
outcomes.must_not_claim: API credential failure.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect with a trusted client certificate.

outcomes.condition: QUIC/TLS handshake exceeds FERRUM_FRONTEND_TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.

public_signal.transport: QUIC close [h3: app close code 0, reason 'handshake timeout' (0-RTT path); full-handshake path drops the future (quinn default code, undetermined)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The QUIC/TLS handshake did not complete within the gateway's handshake timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Certificate rejection.
outcomes.remediation: Check UDP path and client TLS.

outcomes.condition: HTTP/3 frontend: backend read error, size overflow, deadline after DATA, or auth expiry after DATA.

public_signal.transport: RESET_STREAM on the response send half; never a clean FIN [h3: H3_INTERNAL_ERROR (0x102) RESET_STREAM]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The HTTP/3 response stream was reset after it started; the body is incomplete.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, or the cause.
outcomes.remediation: Treat as incomplete.
outcomes.notes: Truncation is distinguishable from EOF on H3.

outcomes.condition: Gateway answered (incl. rejects) and no longer needs the request body.

public_signal.transport: STOP_SENDING after the response is written [h3: STOP_SENDING H3_NO_ERROR (0x100)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server stopped reading the request body after answering; this is not an error.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A failure.
outcomes.remediation: None.
outcomes.notes: Not an error; clients must not treat it as failure.

outcomes.condition: HTTP/3 request HEADERS not received within FERRUM_HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.

public_signal.transport: stream dropped [h3: STOP_SENDING(0) from quinn drop]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server abandoned the HTTP/3 request stream because headers did not arrive in time.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Send headers promptly.
outcomes.notes: docs/http3.md:1460-1467.

outcomes.condition: Request field section larger than advertised SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE, or a non-DATA frame declaring more than 2x that.

public_signal.transport: 431 from h3 library; frame over-declaration closes the connection [h3: H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD (0x0107) connection error for an over-declared frame length]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The request headers exceeded the HTTP/3 field-section limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend rejection.
outcomes.remediation: Reduce header size.
outcomes.notes: Below the h3 cap Ferrum's own 431 JSON applies.

outcomes.condition: HTTP/3 plain CONNECT or unsupported :protocol; CONNECT-UDP disabled or sent in 0-RTT.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"CONNECT method is not allowed"} | {"error":"CONNECT-UDP over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway"} | {"error":"CONNECT-UDP is not allowed in 0-RTT early data"}
public_signal.transport: H3 response or stream reset [h3: H3_MESSAGE_ERROR stream reset for an unregistered :protocol (h3 library)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway does not allow this CONNECT/extended CONNECT form over HTTP/3.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Route absence.
outcomes.remediation: Use a supported protocol.

outcomes.condition: RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP pre-tunnel refusals.

public_signal.body_shape: 400 {"error":"CONNECT-UDP requires the :authority pseudo-header"} (and similar, connect_udp.rs:316-480) | 403 {"error":"CONNECT-UDP target is not an allowed destination for this route"} | 503 {"error":"CONNECT-UDP session limit exceeded"} | 502 {"error":"CONNECT-UDP target could not be resolved"} | 504 {"error":"CONNECT-UDP target resolution timed out"} | 502 {"error":"CONNECT-UDP tunnel socket could not be created"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the CONNECT-UDP tunnel request for the reason in the body.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure unless the body says resolution/socket failure.
outcomes.remediation: Act on the body reason.
outcomes.notes: Established tunnel faults reset with H3_MESSAGE_ERROR / H3_INTERNAL_ERROR (connect_udp.rs:2637, 2789).

outcomes.condition: spec_expose plugin cannot fetch the upstream spec, or is busy.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway's spec_expose plugin could not serve the API specification right now.
outcomes.must_not_claim: API failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry after the indicated delay.
outcomes.notes: The only gateway-originated Retry-After found on the proxy data path; core overload/CB/concurrency/rate-limit/WS/H3 rejects send none. Fetch-failure status can vary.

outcomes.condition: Proxy has >=1 applicable auth plugin, no principal (Consumer or external identity) was committed, and no plugin produced a Reject (Multi) / every applicable plugin returned Continue (Single). Typical: no credential at all (every mechanism extracted Missing: absent header/query, foreign Authorization scheme for jwt/jwks/oauth2/basic, mtls_auth without a client cert); a jwks_auth/oauth2_introspection/oidc credential that validated but had no non-blank identity claim; a valid OIDC session lacking the identity claim; soap_ws_security identity config passing through (mixed_route, or reject_missing_security_header=false).

other_headers.WWW-Authenticate: exactly one value: first authentication_challenge() among applicable auth plugins in ascending priority -> 'Bearer' (oauth2_introspection) | 'Basic realm="ferrum-edge", charset="UTF-8"' (ldap_auth, basic_auth) | literal fallback 'ferrum-edge'
other_headers.Set-Cookie: Multi mode only: cookies staged by earlier rejecting attempts (only oidc_relying_party stages); Single mode drops them

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its (proxy auth phase) plugin produced this outcome; the condition is: Proxy has >=1 applicable auth plugin, no principal (Consumer or external identity) was committed, and no plugin produced a Reject (Multi) / every applicable plugin returned Continue (Single). Built-in rules are monitor-only unless default_rule_action/rule_modes/rule_overrides opt them in; custom_rules default to enforce under mode=enforce. mode=enforce with no reachable enforcement path is a construction error. A confirmed enforcing hit rejects even when the scan also exceeded scan_budget_ms. v0.9.7 (issue #5528): the request/response body and WebSocket-message scan now always runs to completion (run_body_scan_with_budget, src/plugins/waf/mod.rs:633, is post-hoc only and its clock starts after the pre-scan fairness yield), and finish_scan (src/plugins/waf/mod.rs:686) lets hits decide before on_scan_timeout, so an enforcing hit found over budget always rejects. v0.9.5 bailed out BEFORE the body scan when scheduler delay at that yield already exceeded scan_budget_ms: the body was then never inspected and, under the default on_scan_timeout=log_and_allow, was forwarded (a load-dependent miss of this outcome); under block it got the timeout 403 instead (same bytes). On a WebSocket route the upgrade request is rejected with this same HTTP response. Status/body operator-configurable (default 403). Public reason detail: None. Status/body/content-type are static configured values. Rule id, category, severity, target, score go only to transaction metadata (waf.rule_hits, waf.first_blocking_rule, waf.block_reason=rule|score, waf.target, waf.severity, waf.score, waf.instances.<id>.score) and optional log_to_stdout warn logs; no X-WAF-* header. Distinguishability: Byte-identical to bot_detection default reject. outcomes.notes: Each bucket charged at most once per request across before_proxy and final-body recheck. Public reason detail: Discloses configured max_requests and bucket identity (type or operation name). Distinguishability: No Retry-After header emitted. v0.9.7 (#5692): with limit_by=consumer the rate key is tagged 'consumer:<identity>' (or 'ip:<client_ip>' when no identity), so a consumer identity equal to an IP string no longer shares the anonymous budget of that IP; local and Redis counters restart once after upgrade. v0.9.7 Redis-mode counting (rate_limiting/graphql/grpc_method_router request quotas, src/plugins/utils/rate_limit.rs:2447 check_http_windows_redis): each window is 16 sub-buckets; a decision sums the charged sub-bucket, the 17 before it and the one after (each at face value, floored at 0), charges every window in one MULTI/EXEC ending in TIME, refuses when the count including this request exceeds the limit (:2594), and hands the charge back on EVERY window after a refusal (:2620), so refused requests no longer consume budget (the v0.9.5 multi-window phantom increment is gone) and a burst at the end of a window is counted in full. Consequence: a client sending at exactly its configured rate is throttled to at least limit/(limit+ceil(3*limit/16)) admitted (50% at limit 1, 80% at 8); v0.9.5 used a two-window weighted estimate (different boundary timing). Redis counters move to new keys ({prefix:rate-key}:{window_seconds}:{sub_index}), so an in-place upgrade restarts counting (up to one window of reduced enforcement; mixed-version replicas count separately).

outcomes.notes: Header names are lowercase x-ratelimit-limit / x-ratelimit-remaining / x-ratelimit-window; there are NO RateLimit-* (IETF) or Retry-After headers. When several rate_limiting instances are composed, the refusing instance owns the published header set. Native gRPC: rendered by normalize_reject_response_with_provenance (src/proxy/mod.rs:25802) as HTTP 200, content-type application/grpc, trailers-only; grpc-status mapped from HTTP status via http_reject_status_to_grpc_status (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307); grpc-message = body JSON 'error' value. 429 -> grpc-status 8 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, grpc-message 'Rate limit exceeded'; x-ratelimit-* kept in the trailers-only header map. WebSocket: refused at the upgrade handshake as a plain HTTP 429. TCP/UDP: see plugin.rate_limiting.stream_refused. Public reason detail: No limiter key/identity is exposed (x-ratelimit-identity is stripped from requests and responses). Limit and window are exposed only when expose_headers=true. Distinguishability: Same body as the local-capacity 429 (which never carries x-ratelimit-* headers). Different body from graphql 429 ({"errors":[...]}), grpc_method_router 429 and ai_rate_limiter. No Retry-After header is ever set by this plugin. gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307 mapping. v0.9.7 Redis-mode counting (rate_limiting/graphql/grpc_method_router request quotas, src/plugins/utils/rate_limit.rs:2447 check_http_windows_redis): each window is 16 sub-buckets; a decision sums the charged sub-bucket, the 17 before it and the one after (each at face value, floored at 0), charges every window in one MULTI/EXEC ending in TIME, refuses when the count including this request exceeds the limit (:2594), and hands the charge back on EVERY window after a refusal (:2620), so refused requests no longer consume budget (the v0.9.5 multi-window phantom increment is gone) and a burst at the end of a window is counted in full. Consequence: a client sending at exactly its configured rate is throttled to at least limit/(limit+ceil(3*limit/16)) admitted (50% at limit 1, 80% at 8); v0.9.5 used a two-window weighted estimate (different boundary timing). Redis counters move to new keys ({prefix:rate-key}:{window_seconds}:{sub_index}), so an in-place upgrade restarts counting (up to one window of reduced enforcement; mixed-version replicas count separately). During a Redis outage the v0.9.7 default (redis_failure_policy=local_fallback) produces this same 429 from a per-process budget instead of the v0.9.5 default 503.

public_signal.body_shape: (empty; trailers-only) - HTTP 429 {"error":"Rate limit exceeded for gRPC method '{full_method}'"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its grpc_method_router plugin produced this outcome; the condition is: Per-method rate limit (method_rate_limits) exhausted.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend application produced this response (unless the destination is not a trusted Ferrum endpoint, in which case the body alone proves nothing); the exact quota window or that other callers share the limit unless headers say so.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: slow down and honour any rate-limit headers present before retrying.
outcomes.notes: Native gRPC: rendered by normalize_reject_response_with_provenance (src/proxy/mod.rs:25802) as HTTP 200, content-type application/grpc, trailers-only; grpc-status mapped from HTTP status via http_reject_status_to_grpc_status (src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307); grpc-message = body JSON 'error' value. Public reason detail: Method name and limit disclosed. Distinguishability: Only source of x-grpc-ratelimit-* headers. gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307 mapping. v0.9.7 (#5692): with limit_by=consumer the rate key is tagged 'consumer:<identity>' (or 'ip:<client_ip>' when no identity), so a consumer identity equal to an IP string no longer shares the anonymous budget of that IP; local and Redis counters restart once after upgrade. v0.9.7 Redis-mode counting (rate_limiting/graphql/grpc_method_router request quotas, src/plugins/utils/rate_limit.rs:2447 check_http_windows_redis): each window is 16 sub-buckets; a decision sums the charged sub-bucket, the 17 before it and the one after (each at face value, floored at 0), charges every window in one MULTI/EXEC ending in TIME, refuses when the count including this request exceeds the limit (:2594), and hands the charge back on EVERY window after a refusal (:2620), so refused requests no longer consume budget (the v0.9.5 multi-window phantom increment is gone) and a burst at the end of a window is counted in full. Consequence: a client sending at exactly its configured rate is throttled to at least limit/(limit+ceil(3*limit/16)) admitted (50% at limit 1, 80% at 8); v0.9.5 used a two-window weighted estimate (different boundary timing). Redis counters move to new keys ({prefix:rate-key}:{window_seconds}:{sub_index}), so an in-place upgrade restarts counting (up to one window of reduced enforcement; mixed-version replicas count separately).

source.symbol: retry loop stops once the route deadline expired

outcomes.condition: Non-gRPC request on a mesh_route_dispatch rule with request_timeout_ms (Gateway API HTTPRoute rules[].timeouts.request projects onto it); the total deadline expired while an attempt that had already been handed to the backend (after buffered client-body collection, request-body hooks, DNS and backend admission) was still waiting for the response head or for buffered response-body collection. The attempt is cancelled (RouteDeadlineExpiry::InFlight with the handoff marker set; every retry attempt counts as handed over from its first poll).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports the route's total request deadline (HTTPRoute timeouts.request / mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms) ran out before a response head was available; the response does not say which phase used the time or whether the backend received the request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend was slow or received the request (the deadline also spans gateway-side phases, the client upload and retry backoff), which phase expired, the configured duration, or that the request is safe to replay.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator / API owner: compare the rule's timeouts.request with backend latency plus client upload time and retry backoff; the gateway transaction log records metadata route_request_timeout = dispatch | before_dispatch | retry_backoff (src/plugins/mod.rs:268, :4482). Retry only idempotent requests.
outcomes.notes: v0.9.6+ only (no route deadline exists at v0.9.5; default: none). X-Gateway-Error comes from status 504 alone (src/retry.rs:281). The deadline is anchored at request receipt (RequestContext::new, src/plugins/mod.rs:3847) and armed after before_proxy selects the rule (src/proxy/mod.rs:32949, re-armed :33206). Never retried: the retry loop breaks on it (:38133) and should_retry refuses DispatchPolicyRejected. gRPC-flavoured requests never get this body: the route budget is folded into the RPC deadline and ends with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (gRPC slice). The native HTTP/3 frontend refuses non-gRPC requests on such rules with 503 {"error":"Route request timeout is not supported over HTTP/3"} (src/http3/server.rs:18297, H3 slice), and Alt-Svc is withheld on every frontend port serving such a rule (src/proxy/mod.rs:10649), so this 504 is an HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 outcome. The route timeout 504 is built with an empty header map exactly like the Backend timeout 504. The body is a fixed literal a backend can also send. On a timed route it can pre-empt size.request_body_read_timeout (408) and buffered-body timeouts, since buffered client-body collection and buffered response collection run inside the deadline-wrapped attempt. This variant is charged to the backend (circuit breaker, passive health, latency sample); transaction-log phase "dispatch". No Content-Type header on the HTTP/1.1 / HTTP/2 path: built with an empty header map (src/proxy/mod.rs:49270 route_request_timeout_response (headers: HashMap::new())), like the other backend-failure bodies.

outcomes.condition: Non-gRPC request on a mesh_route_dispatch rule with attempt_timeout_ms (Gateway API timeouts.backendRequest projects onto both attempt_timeout_ms and timeout_ms); the attempt's budget, started when the attempt was handed to the backend (after buffered client-body collection, request-body hooks, DNS and admission; for a streamed upload the upload time after handoff counts), expired before the response head or before buffered response-body collection finished, while the route's total deadline had not.

Retryable like any 504: each retry gets a fresh budget; Gateway API retry replays it only if 504 is in codes and the method is GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/DELETE (src/config_sources/k8s/gateway_api.rs:7073, src/config/types.rs:2367, src/retry.rs:1846), always within the total timeouts.request. gRPC folds the budget into its RPC deadline (gRPC slice); native HTTP/3 refuses such rules with 503 (H3 slice). After the head, the same budget cuts the body (streaming.route_deadline_cut_after_headers). outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Response headers arrived but the response body did not complete; the transfer was cut by the gateway or upstream after the status was sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the response is complete or successful because the status was 2xx, that the backend stalled (a route deadline also ends healthy long responses), which cause applied, or that a non-idempotent request is safe to replay.
outcomes.remediation: Treat the result as incomplete; retry only idempotent requests; gateway operator: size the route's timeouts.request / timeouts.backendRequest for the longest complete response the rule must serve and correlate gateway logs (body_error_class read_write_timeout).
outcomes.notes: v0.9.6+ only. Never retried (head already committed). Health-neutral for the backend; the deferred log keeps body_error_class read_write_timeout without a client-disconnect flag. gRPC requests fold the deadlines into the RPC deadline instead (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED trailers, gRPC slice); the native HTTP/3 frontend never serves such rules.

source.symbol: handle_h3_request route-timeout refusal gate (Plain flavor only)

outcomes.condition: Native HTTP/3 plain request (not gRPC, not gRPC-Web, not WebSocket, not CONNECT-UDP) matched a route rule that sets a total request timeout (Gateway API HTTPRoute timeouts.request / mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms) or a per-attempt timeout (timeouts.backendRequest / attempt_timeout_ms). Refused after route match, before target selection, circuit-breaker admission or any dial.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Route request timeout is not supported over HTTP/3"}
public_signal.transport: H3 response (HEADERS + DATA + FIN), then the request side is halted with STOP_SENDING(H3_NO_ERROR) (stream_util.rs:364). Initial response-header policy plugins may add headers (server.rs:17594).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused this HTTP/3 request because its route carries a request/attempt timeout the gateway cannot enforce over HTTP/3; the same request over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 is served under that timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend unavailability, overload or a circuit breaker (nothing was dialed), or that the route itself is broken.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: retry over HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 (stop forcing h3 / drop a cached Alt-Svc). Operator: remove the rule timeout or accept that HTTP/3 is not served for that route.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.6 (released v0.9.7); route rule timeouts do not exist in v0.9.5. The call passes grpc_status 14 and grpc-message 'Route request timeout is not supported over HTTP/3' to the flavor-aware writer, but the gate requires HttpFlavor::Plain and gRPC-Web is re-flavored Grpc on H3 (server.rs:2397), so no gRPC/gRPC-Web caller can receive it: those fold the budget into their RPC deadline (protocol.grpc.client_deadline_exceeded). No X-Gateway-Error. Transaction-log rejection phase 'route_request_timeout_unsupported'. Runs before the deferred before_proxy pass, so a deferred response_mock / fault_injection abort is answered with this 503 over H3 where H1/H2 return the mock. Alt-Svc is withheld on EVERY H1/H2 response of a frontend port that serves such a rule (per config generation; a Global-scope mesh_route_dispatch instance or a port-agnostic proxy withholds it on all ports), so only clients that reach HTTP/3 on their own see this. Do not confuse with H3's pre-existing 408 {"error":"Request timeout"} (cross_protocol.rs:2379) or the new H1/H2 504 {"error":"Request timeout"} (mod.rs:48962).

outcomes.condition: Mesh inbound HBONE CONNECT (byte or datagram tunnel) whose peer is not admitted: no authenticated mesh peer identity (v0.9.5 and later), or, new in v0.9.6+, an authenticated peer whose retained certificate chain no longer verifies against the inbound admission trust in force (trust bundle rotation) or is revoked by the enforced CRL set. Refused before any upstream is selected or dialed.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"HBONE tunnel requires an authenticated mesh peer"} | {"error":"HBONE UDP tunnel requires an authenticated mesh peer"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The destination gateway did not admit the mesh peer for an HBONE tunnel (missing authenticated identity, or a credential no longer trusted/valid there).
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which admission check failed (identity missing, trust anchor, or revocation): the bodies are byte-identical by design; the cause is only in the destination's log (mesh_authz.deny_policy / rejection phase).
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: check the peer's SVID, trust bundle distribution and CRLs on the destination; destination log reason hbone_unauthenticated_peer | hbone_peer_trust_withdrawn | hbone_peer_revoked (udp: hbone_udp_*).
outcomes.notes: Mesh-only (peer is another mesh proxy, not an API client). The bodies are NOT new in v0.9.7: v0.9.5 already emitted them for an unauthenticated peer (v0.9.5 hbone_proxy.rs:629 / 1216); v0.9.7 adds the credential-admission trigger (#5568/#5574) with the identical body. The drift entry 'HBONE tunnels without an authenticated mesh peer now 403' overstates the change. Successful CONNECT 200s may now carry x-ferrum-mesh-tunnel-reuse: fenced (hbone_proxy.rs:1411; capability only, spoofable marker).

outcomes.condition: Mesh inbound HBONE: an established byte or datagram tunnel is cut by the admission-fence sweep that runs on config/trust/CRL/PeerAuthentication publications when the tunnel would no longer be admitted (proxy_withdrawn, peer_expired, peer_trust, peer_revoked, authorization_denied, peer_auth_transport, relay_destination, reuse_withdrawn, reevaluation_failed).

public_signal.transport: tunnel ends without a reason: the relay drops the upgraded HTTP/2 CONNECT stream and the local backend socket (stream-level end chosen by hyper/h2, not by the gateway); the UDP relay drops without shutdown(), same as an idle expiry

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The mesh tunnel ended without an in-band reason; the destination may have revoked its admission after a policy or credential change.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific revocation reason or that the backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: destination log 'HBONE tunnel closed: admission revoked' with reason; reconnect opens a fresh CONNECT under current policy.
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.6+ (issue #5042 step 1). v0.9.5 tunnels outlived later policy/trust changes. Byte-tunnel first failure is a ConnectionAborted io error with message 'HBONE tunnel terminated: mesh admission revoked by a later policy generation' (classified connection_closed, retry.rs:940); the datagram relay logs body_error_class connection_closed.

outcomes.condition: Introspection provider answered active=true (and passed the cnf, token_type, issuer and audience checks) but returned an integer nbf later than the gateway clock (no leeway). Checked before exp, so it also wins over an elapsed exp. Such responses are never cached; positive-cache hits re-check the window. A JSON null nbf is treated as absent; a non-integer nbf is 503 introspection_unavailable instead.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its oauth2_introspection plugin produced this outcome; the condition is: Introspection provider answered active=true (and passed the cnf, token_type, issuer and audience checks) but returned an integer nbf later than the gateway clock (no leeway). Checked before exp, so it also wins over an elapsed exp. Such responses are never cached; positive-cache hits re-check the window. A JSON null nbf is treated as absent; a non-integer nbf is 503 introspection_unavailable instead.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend application produced this response (unless the destination is not a trusted Ferrum endpoint, in which case the body alone proves nothing); that the token is revoked or inactive (the provider reported it active); whether the token was pre-minted or the authorization server and gateway clocks disagree.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: retry after the token's not-before time; if it persists, the operator should check clock synchronization between the authorization server and the gateway (no leeway is applied).
outcomes.notes: New in v0.9.7 (issue #5523); no such body in v0.9.5, which ignored introspection nbf. In fan-out mode a candidate's unavailability (503) outranks this decision, and the first auth decision among candidates wins. Public reason detail: not-yet-valid window. Distinguishability: Unique body. gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307 mapping.

outcomes.condition: REGISTRY_ONLY egress (auto-injected __mesh_outbound_registry scoped to the outbound capture listener ports, or an operator-configured mesh_outbound_registry, unscoped by default) and the HTTP-family request's Host/:authority host[:port] is not in the registry (bare host, host:port, host:*, or one-label *.suffix wildcard), on a listener not stamped Inbound.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its mesh_outbound_registry plugin refused the request before dispatch; the condition is: REGISTRY_ONLY egress (auto-injected __mesh_outbound_registry scoped to the outbound capture listener ports, or an operator-configured mesh_outbound_registry, unscoped by default) and the HTTP-family request's Host/:authority host[:port] is not in the registry (bare host, host:port, host:*, or one-label *.suffix wildcard), on a listener not stamped Inbound.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the destination or backend is down or was contacted (nothing was dispatched); that credentials are invalid; that the body proves a Ferrum gateway produced it (backend-spoofable).
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: register the destination (Service/ServiceEntry or registry entry, including the port the client uses) or relax outboundTrafficPolicy; the caller cannot fix this by retrying.
outcomes.notes: Not new in v0.9.7: the same reject existed in v0.9.5 (src/plugins/mesh/outbound_registry.rs:521/531, sha 20e7603) but was not catalogued in ferrum-edge-0.9.5. v0.9.7 change (PR #5595): requests stamped with the Inbound mesh direction are never enforced, even for unscoped operator-managed instances or when an inbound listener shares the outbound capture port number; v0.9.5 could return this reject for such inbound traffic. Runs in on_request_received (before auth). Status configurable 400-599 (plugin reject_status; mesh FERRUM_MESH_OUTBOUND_REGISTRY_REJECT_STATUS, default 502). No X-Gateway-Error (plugin reject path, src/proxy/mod.rs:25802 normalize_reject_response_with_provenance adds none). gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307 mapping (502 -> 14). Distinguishability: unique body; unlike backend 502s it carries no X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Same enforcement scope as destination_not_registered, but the request carries no Host header (HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and gRPC backfill :authority into host, so in practice an HTTP/1.0-style request without Host).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its mesh_outbound_registry plugin refused the request before dispatch; the condition is: Same enforcement scope as destination_not_registered, but the request carries no Host header (HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and gRPC backfill :authority into host, so in practice an HTTP/1.0-style request without Host).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the destination or backend is down or was contacted; that credentials are invalid.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send a Host header naming a registered destination.

No X-Gateway-Error (plugin reject path, src/proxy/mod.rs:25802 normalize_reject_response_with_provenance adds none). gRPC status derived from src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2307 mapping (502 -> 14).

outcomes.condition: An enabled response_transformer instance (rules_enabled) is on the chain: with any static header/body rule it declares ResponseTrailerPolicy::Unbounded, so trailer-forwarding response paths drop the whole backend trailer section on every request; a rules-free apply_route_overrides consumer (the instance the Gateway API / Istio translators emit) declares RequestConditionalUnbounded and drops trailers only when the matched mesh_route_dispatch rule published a response-header override for this request.

public_signal.body_shape: (response otherwise normal) backend trailer section dropped on trailer-forwarding paths

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, a response_transformer (response-header policy) on this route may have removed the backend's trailer section; the missing trailers do not by themselves identify which plugin or rule did it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend omitted the trailers; which exact rule/policy matched; that the response was otherwise modified.
outcomes.remediation: Check the gateway plugin configuration for this route.
outcomes.notes: Not new behaviour for operator-authored instances: v0.9.5 (src/plugins/response_transformer.rs:1261@20e7603) already declared Unbounded for every enabled instance, including rules-free route-override consumers, but the v0.9.5 catalog has no record for it. v0.9.7 change: the rules-free apply_route_overrides consumer is request-conditional, so a request whose matched rule published no ResponseHeaderModifier (e.g. a sibling Gateway API rule merged onto the same proxy) now keeps its backend trailers. Per ResponseTrailerPolicy docs the trailer-forwarding paths are buffered and streaming native HTTP/3; exact per-frontend effect not traced. Public reason detail: None. Distinguishability: Observable only as missing backend trailers; indistinguishable from plugin.waf.response_trailers_dropped.
